key_insight: Classical feasibility repair can recover useful quantum sampling bias by aggregating infeasible outputs into feasible solutions.
engineering_relevance: Post-measurement repair offers a practical way to improve constrained quantum optimization without discarding infeasible samples.
method: Construct problem-dependent repair maps from constraint-violation statistics.
Push the raw sampling distribution onto feasible solutions, aggregating probability over each repair basin.
For permutation constraints, use O(n³) Hungarian maximum-overlap repair.
evidence_signal: For one n=10 TSP simulation, repair recovered the optimum in approximately 10³ shots versus 10⁶ without repair; tests on a 127-qubit IBM processor used encodings up to 100 qubits.
watch_item: Benefits depend on quantum probability concentrating in useful repair basins; these results do not establish general quantum advantage.
paper_title: Leaving Quantum Bias on the Table: Pushforwards as a Path to Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization
